title: The Lanes at night
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Wood walks past the bowling alley at night for no reason he'll give. The sign, all letters lit. The dumpster round back. He doesn't go round back. Not yet.

panels.composition: SMALL WOOD LANES across 101 at night, the neon on the roofline all lit, three pickups, rain. WOOD on the far shoulder.

image.prompt: a small-town bowling alley seen across a two-lane highway at night with its neon sign fully lit and three pickups in the lot, a young man on the far shoulder in rain, black and white, no words
image.notes: All fifteen letters lit (objects.md: all lit 1998–2008).

panels.composition: The sign. Every letter. Drawn carefully, as a thing that will change.

image.prompt: close on a neon bowling alley sign on a roofline with every letter glowing, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood looking down the alley beside the building toward the back. The chain-link. The bulb. He doesn't go.

image.prompt: a young man looking down a dark alley beside a bowling alley toward a bare bulb over a chain-link fence, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood walking on toward town. The sign behind him, all lit. Three weeks.

image.prompt: a young man walking away along a highway shoulder at night with a fully lit neon sign behind him, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Three weeks before the dog. He doesn't go round back yet.
